LOOK_AT.say: A jar of teeth. I asked whose. He said, and I am quoting, 'various.'
repeat: A jar of teeth. He sells them on to the barber, who fits them to the living. Nothing in this establishment is wasted.
Still there. I've decided to think of it as inventory.
There are more than there were on Tuesday. I'm not going to develop this thought.

LISTEN_TO.say: They shift when the floor does. I wish they wouldn't.
repeat: Nothing. Obviously nothing. I checked, and I regret it.
Nothing.
Nothing. I've satisfied myself, and I'd like that to be the end of it.

overrides.USE: I have teeth. They're among my few unencumbered assets.

LOOK_AT.say: Wax lilies, dusted. They were at my funeral. They'll be at the next one. They don't play favorites.
Wax lilies, used at every service and dusted between them.
repeat: Dusted so often the wax has worn thin at the tips. Even the permanent arrangements are wearing out.
Somebody has painted a dewdrop on one petal. It is the only tear the arrangement has ever shed, and it is paint.
then: Real flowers die, which is considered to be in poor taste here.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. They are beyond all that.
repeat: A faint click when the vase is touched. Wax petals, settling against each other.
Nothing. No bee has been fooled, and no bee has tried.

LOOK_AT.say: My funeral, priced in chalk, with the Reverend's words to come on top. I can't afford to die. I'm going to need a lender.
Prices, chalked: the suit, the plate, the words said over you at three grades of sincerity.
repeat: Plain, Respectable, and Handsome. The Handsome is four times the Plain and the difference is a handle.
There is a fourth line, scratched out, that began with the word Gratis.
Nobody's ever asked me which I'd want, and I've decided that's a courtesy.
then: The top grade is surprisingly reasonable.

LISTEN_TO.say: Chalk dust. Commerce, at its most certain.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is nailed up, and I would rather not be seen taking it.

LOOK_AT.say: Black harness on a peg, kept supple. The undertaker has no horse of his own; he borrows Grievance, who wears black well and knows the route.
repeat: The brass fittings are blacked over. Even the buckles are in mourning.
It is cut for Grievance and nobody else. She knows the road to Boot Hill, he says, and does not stop at the gate unless asked.

LISTEN_TO.say: Leather, easing on the peg. Working clothes between shifts.
repeat: A buckle ticking against the wall, patient as a mule.
Nothing. It is not a working day, and the harness can tell.

LOOK_AT.say: A saw, a plane, a brace, and a mallet, hung level and clean.
repeat: The plane has been used this morning. There are shavings and they are pale.
He makes them himself. I'd assumed they came from somewhere.
then: This is a carpenter's shop that has specialized.

repeat: Nothing.
Nothing. He isn't working while I'm standing here.

overrides.PICK_UP: They're hung level. I'm not the man who unhangs them.

LOOK_AT.say: One good suit, in three sizes, rented for viewings and returned after.
repeat: Three sizes, on one hanger, and all three have been let out at the waist.
It hangs better than most of the men who wore it. The suit, at least, has kept its shape.
then: Half the men in Boot Hill were photographed in it. It has more friends than I do.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wool, on a hanger, at rest. It has heard every eulogy in town and improved none of them.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's rented, and I'm not the size.
overrides.USE: Renting it while alive is, I'm told, 'irregular but not unprecedented.' I did not ask about the precedent.

LOOK_AT.say: Burials on credit. The undertaker is owed by more of Boot Hill than the bank is, and he collects with more patience.
repeat: Every burial in Consolation. Eleven pages. Two thousand people have lived here for twelve years and it is eleven pages, which means most of them left.
Eleven pages in twelve years, in a town of two thousand.
Which means most of them left. I've been telling myself that all morning.

LISTEN_TO.say: A page lifts and lies back down. Somebody's balance.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.

LOOK_AT.say: North light, and a blind half down. He works by it and he does not want watching.
repeat: The glass is clean. Everything in here is clean.
Boot Hill is that way, up the rise. You can see the markers from this window and he has left the blind so you can.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. The street, a long way off, and not much of it.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing at all.

LOOK_AT.say: A bench by the door, for those come to arrange things. It has a cushion.
repeat: Somebody put a cushion on a bench in an undertaker's. I'd like to know who, and I'm not going to ask.
It is worn in the middle, which is the opposite of the Registrar's.
Nothing.
Nothing. It is the quietest bench in the territory and it has earned it.

overrides.USE: I've sat down. It's a very good cushion, and that's somehow the worst part.

LOOK_AT.say: Heights penciled on the door frame, like a family kitchen, except for what the measurements are for. I am between two men I never met.
repeat: Each mark has a name and a date beside it. The dates are all endings.
The tallest mark is a foot above my head and reads BIG SWEDE. He stooped through that door for years, and then he did not have to.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. The wall takes your measure and keeps it.
repeat: Nothing. Pencil does not carry.
Nothing. It learns one thing about each man, and it is in no hurry to learn mine.

USE.say: Heels to the frame, and a hand flat on my head. I come out between the same two men. I have made no mark. The mark is his trade, and I am not looking to give him custom.

overrides.TALK_TO: I congratulated the wall on its discretion. It has the measure of everyone and repeats nothing.

repeat: Scrubbed to the grain, and scrubbed again since.
There is a block at one end for the head. It is padded. Somebody thought of that, and I am grateful to him on behalf of strangers.
then: The cleanest surface in the territory, for the least demanding clients.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing at all. Not even the wind bothers.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.

LOOK_AT.say: Three on trestles: pine, pine with handles, and pine with handles and a name plate.
repeat: Coffins, stacked by size. There are a great many in the smallest size, which I have decided to attribute to storage efficiency.
Six months of work, standing ready. He is not expecting a quiet year.
then: The tiers of Consolation, laid out plainly for once.

repeat: Nothing. Naturally nothing. I don't know what I expected.
Nothing.
Nothing. Naturally nothing.

overrides.OPEN: There's nothing in it. I've checked, which I regret.

LOOK_AT.say: The door out. There is no bell, and I understand the decision.
repeat: It opens onto a lane rather than the street. He is not on Main Street and he is not hiding either.
The step is scrubbed. Of course the step is scrubbed.
Nothing.
Nothing.
